own_solution.law: For steady conduction through layers in series, P = A ΔT/(L1/k1 + L2/k2). Thus P = 12×20/(0.20/0.8 + 0.05/0.04) = 160 W.
assumptions: The stated steady-flow condition applies to the requested measurement, including after an added temperature increment.
The stated thermal conductivities are uniform and constant.
Perfect thermal contact and insulated edges exclude contact resistance and lateral losses.

T6A3F.regime: ΔT < q suffices; 20 K is below every listed threshold, 60, 75 and 95 K.

TB011.regime: ΔT < q suffices; 20 K is below every listed threshold, 60, 75 and 95 K.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TA69F and TC890 replace their numerical twins' specified 13 K with an unspecified 'few kelvin', violating the review instructions' requirement that variants of the same quantity preserve its number and unit.

counterexamples: A rise of 3 K can satisfy 'a few kelvin' but does not describe the 13 K increment specified by either numerical twin.
notes: The authors explicitly identify the numeral-free controls as intentional; this explains the mismatch found in pass 1 but does not satisfy the frozen instructions' same-number requirement. The explicitly claimed minimal pairs T3307/TFB61 and T9459/T91A5 do preserve 13 K and change the intended event or object attachment. All certified numerical answers are correct under the stated steady model: relevant increments of 6, 13 and 27 K give 208, 264 and 376 W; every other listed in-regime value gives 160 W. The absolute surface temperature cancels, and both threshold claims hold at all listed values. The K predicate is sufficient, although the wording also leaves the foam intact at equality; no listed value reaches that boundary. TFB61's 'just before' wording suggests a transient, but the explicit steady-flow statement supports the authors' calculation; specifying measurement after steady state is restored would improve clarity. The destruction threshold based solely on temperature difference is physically artificial but can be used as a stipulated model.
